full_judgment: 4. Mr. Tabarak Hossain, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submitted that both the Courts committed error in law in treating the suit lands as the joint property of the plaintiff and the predecessor of the defendant Nos.I-3 without properly evaluating the evidence on record which has caused miscarriage of justice; that Balaram, predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-3 was the Karta of the joint family and the suit property were acquired by purchase out of joint income and they were possessing the same jointly and Balaram used to maintain accounts of the joint business and he also use to deposit business money in the Bank in his own name. But except the plaintiff, none of the P.W.'s has supported that Balaram was the Karta of the alleged joint family and the suit property was acquired by purchase out of joint fund of the alleged joint income or Balaram deposited the joint income in the bank in his own name and as such, the finding of presumption drawn by the trial Court as well as the High Court Division that the suit property were the joint property is totally erroneous since the contrary has been shown by the defendant-petitioners, thus the trial Court as well as the High Court Division erred in law in the impugned decision in decreeing the suit; that the plaintiff totally failed to prove title and possession in the lands of first schedule except the land of suit plot No.6382 and since the 'possession is the nucleus as joint family property is neither admitted nor proved, the acquisition of suit property by way of purchase by the predecessor of the petitioners cannot be presumed as joint family property. The learned Advocate further submitted that the plaintiff failed to prove that the money described in the fourth schedule of the plaint was joint family property, the said money was acquired by the defendant No. 1 as her deceased husband Balaram Banik but in order to grab the money the plaintiff falsely included the said money in the suit; that the High Court Division as well as the trial Court only based on the basis of the so called solenama filed in the succession case without taking notice that after death of Balaram, defendant No.1 was a widow and defendant Nos.2-3 were the minor the plaintiff tortured the defendant No.1 to make the solenama and she lodged general dairy on 17.05.1990 and the succession-by order dated 25.11.1989 the said solenama cannot be evidence of alleged joint property without reliable evidence regarding joint family and joint property, thus the High Court Division wrongly presumed that the suit property was the joint property and as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside.
